sanskrit: sūta uvāca tasya kaṇṭham anuprāpto brāhmaṇaḥ saha bhāryayā dahan dīpta ivāṅgāras tam uvācāntarikṣagaḥ
english: Sūta said: A brahmin along with his wife had reached Garuḍa's throat. Garuḍa — blazing like a flaming coal — spoke to him as he flew through the sky.

sanskrit: dvijottama vinirgaccha tūrṇam āsyād apāvṛtāt na hi me brāhmaṇo vadhyaḥ pāpeṣv api rataḥ sadā
english: "O best of twice-born, come out quickly from my open mouth. A brahmin is never to be slain by me, not even one who is always given to wicked deeds."

sanskrit: bruvāṇam evaṃ garuḍaṃ brāhmaṇaḥ samabhāṣata niṣādī mama bhāryeyaṃ nirgacchatu mayā saha
english: As Garuḍa spoke thus, the brahmin addressed him: "This Niṣādī woman is my wife — let her come out together with me."

sanskrit: garuḍa uvāca etām api niṣādīṃ tvaṃ parigṛhyāśu niṣpata tūrṇaṃ saṃbhāvayātmānam ajīrṇaṃ mama tejasā
english: Garuḍa said: "Take this Niṣādī woman too and fly out swiftly. Sustain yourself well — you have not yet been digested by my fierce energy."

sanskrit: sūta uvāca tataḥ sa vipro niṣkrānto niṣādīsahitas tadā vardhayitvā ca garuḍam iṣṭaṃ deśaṃ jagāma ha
english: Sūta said: Then that brahmin came out, accompanied by the Niṣādī woman. Having praised Garuḍa, he departed to his desired destination.

sanskrit: sahabhārye viniṣkrānte tasmin vipre sa pakṣirāṭ vitatya pakṣāv ākāśam utpapāta manojavaḥ
english: When that brahmin had departed with his wife, the king of birds spread his wings and soared into the sky with the speed of thought.

sanskrit: tato 'paśyat sa pitaraṃ pṛṣṭaś cākhyātavān pituḥ ahaṃ hi sarpaiḥ prahitaḥ somam āhartum udyataḥ mātur dāsyavimokṣārtham āhariṣye tam adya vai
english: Then he saw his father and, being questioned, told his father: "I have been sent by the serpents; I am resolved to fetch soma. I shall bring it this very day for the sake of freeing my mother from bondage."

sanskrit: mātrā cāsmi samādiṣṭo niṣādān bhakṣayeti vai na ca me tṛptir abhavad bhakṣayitvā sahasraśaḥ
english: "I was also instructed by my mother to eat Niṣādas. Yet I found no satisfaction even after devouring them by the thousands."

sanskrit: tasmād bhoktavyam aparaṃ bhagavan pradiśasva me yad bhuktvāmṛtam āhartuṃ samarthaḥ syām ahaṃ prabho
english: "Therefore, O blessed one, O lord, point out to me another food that I may eat and thereafter be capable of fetching the amṛta."

sanskrit: kaśyapa uvāca āsīd vibhāvasur nāma maharṣiḥ kopano bhṛśam bhrātā tasyānujaś cāsīt supratīko mahātapāḥ
english: Kaśyapa said: "There was once a great sage named Vibhāvasu, exceedingly wrathful. He had a younger brother named Supratīka, great in his austerities."

sanskrit: sa necchati dhanaṃ bhrātrā sahaikasthaṃ mahāmuniḥ vibhāgaṃ kīrtayaty eva supratīko 'tha nityaśaḥ
english: "That great sage did not wish to hold wealth in common with his brother; Supratīka kept insisting on a partition, again and again."

sanskrit: athābravīc ca taṃ bhrātā supratīkaṃ vibhāvasuḥ vibhāgaṃ bahavo mohāt kartum icchanti nityadā tato vibhaktā anyonyaṃ nādriyante 'rthamohitāḥ
english: "And his brother Vibhāvasu said to Supratīka: 'Many people desire to make a partition out of delusion, always. Once separated, they no longer regard one another, deluded by wealth.'"

sanskrit: tataḥ svārthaparān mūḍhān pṛthag bhūtān svakair dhanaiḥ viditvā bhedayanty etān amitrā mitrarūpiṇaḥ
english: "'Knowing those fools absorbed in self-interest, separated and each with his own wealth, enemies in the guise of friends then drive them further apart.'"

sanskrit: viditvā cāpare bhinnān antareṣu patanty atha bhinnānām atulo nāśaḥ kṣipram eva pravartate
english: "'And others, knowing them to be divided, fall upon the gaps between them. The destruction of the divided is immeasurable and comes about swiftly.'"

sanskrit: tasmāc caiva vibhāgārthaṃ na praśaṃsanti paṇḍitāḥ guruśāstre nibaddhānām anyonyam abhiśaṅkinām
english: "'Therefore the wise do not commend partition for those bound together under the teaching of a guru, who would come to be suspicious of one another.'"

sanskrit: niyantuṃ na hi śakyas tvaṃ bhedato dhanam icchasi yasmāt tasmāt supratīka hastitvaṃ samavāpsyasi
english: "'Since you cannot be restrained and you desire to divide the wealth, therefore, O Supratīka, you shall become an elephant.'"

sanskrit: śaptas tv evaṃ supratīko vibhāvasum athābravīt tvam apy antarjalacaraḥ kacchapaḥ saṃbhaviṣyasi
english: "Cursed thus, Supratīka then spoke to Vibhāvasu: 'You too shall become a tortoise that moves beneath the waters.'"

sanskrit: evam anyonyaśāpāt tau supratīkavibhāvasū gajakacchapatāṃ prāptāv arthārthaṃ mūḍhacetasau
english: "Thus, through mutual curses, Supratīka and Vibhāvasu, their minds foolish on account of wealth, came to assume the forms of an elephant and a tortoise."

sanskrit: roṣadoṣānuṣaṅgeṇa tiryagyonigatāv api parasparadveṣaratau pramāṇabaladarpitau
english: "Even though they had taken birth in animal wombs through the fault of their anger, they were devoted to mutual hatred, both proud of their extraordinary strength."

sanskrit: sarasy asmin mahākāyau pūrvavairānusāriṇau tayor ekataraḥ śrīmān samupaiti mahāgajaḥ
english: "These two with their great bodies, pursuing old enmity, dwell in that lake. One of them, the magnificent great elephant, now approaches."

sanskrit: tasya bṛṃhitaśabdena kūrmo 'py antarjaleśayaḥ utthito 'sau mahākāyaḥ kṛtsnaṃ saṃkṣobhayan saraḥ
english: "Hearing the trumpeting sound of the elephant, the tortoise, that great-bodied one who rests beneath the water, rises up, churning the entire lake."

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvāveṣṭitakaraḥ pataty eṣa gajo jalam dantahastāgralāṅgūlapādavegena vīryavān
english: "Seeing the tortoise, the elephant with its entwined trunk plunges into the water — mighty, with the force of its tusks, trunk, tail, and feet."

sanskrit: taṃ vikṣobhayamāṇaṃ tu saro bahujhaṣākulam kūrmo 'py abhyudyataśirā yuddhāyābhyeti vīryavān
english: "As the elephant churns that lake filled with many fish, the tortoise too raises its head and comes forward mightily, eager for battle."

sanskrit: ṣaḍ ucchrito yojanāni gajas tad dviguṇāyataḥ kūrmas triyojanotsedho daśayojanamaṇḍalaḥ
english: "The elephant stands six yojanas tall and is twice that in length; the tortoise is three yojanas in height and ten yojanas in circumference."

sanskrit: tāv etau yuddhasaṃmattau parasparajayaiṣiṇau upayujyāśu karmedaṃ sādhayepsitam ātmanaḥ
english: "These two, maddened for battle and each seeking victory over the other — make swift use of them and accomplish your desired goal."

sanskrit: sūta uvāca sa tac chrutvā pitur vākyaṃ bhīmavego 'ntarikṣagaḥ nakhena gajam ekena kūrmam ekena cākṣipat
english: Sūta said: Having heard his father's words, the sky-soarer of terrible speed seized the elephant with one talon and the tortoise with the other.

sanskrit: samutpapāta cākāśaṃ tata uccair vihaṃgamaḥ so 'lambatīrtham āsādya devavṛkṣān upāgamat
english: Then that great bird soared high into the sky and, reaching the sacred ford called Ālambatīrtha, he approached the trees of the gods.

sanskrit: te bhītāḥ samakampanta tasya pakṣānilāhatāḥ na no bhañjyād iti tadā divyāḥ kanakaśākhinaḥ
english: Terrified, those divine trees with their golden branches trembled, struck by the wind of his wings, thinking, "Let him not break us."

sanskrit: pracalāṅgān sa tān dṛṣṭvā manorathaphalāṅkurān anyān atularūpāṅgān upacakrāma khecaraḥ
english: Seeing those trees shaking their limbs — trees whose fruits fulfil all desires, with incomparably beautiful forms — the sky-ranger approached others.

sanskrit: kāñcanai rājataiś caiva phalair vaiḍūryaśākhinaḥ sāgarāmbuparikṣiptān bhrājamānān mahādrumān
english: He approached those great and radiant trees, their branches set with vaiḍūrya gems, bearing golden and silver fruits, surrounded by the waters of the ocean.

sanskrit: tam uvāca khagaśreṣṭhaṃ tatra rohiṇapādapaḥ atipravṛddhaḥ sumahān āpatantaṃ manojavam
english: There, the Rohiṇa tree — exceedingly grown and very great — spoke to that best of birds as he came swooping with the speed of thought:

sanskrit: yaiṣā mama mahāśākhā śatayojanam āyatā etām āsthāya śākhāṃ tvaṃ khādemau gajakacchapau
english: "This great branch of mine extends one hundred yojanas. Alight on this branch and devour these two — the elephant and the tortoise."

sanskrit: tato drumaṃ patagasahasrasevitaṃ; mahīdharapratimavapuḥ prakampayan khagottamo drutam abhipatya vegavān; babhañja tām aviralapatrasaṃvṛtām
english: Then, swiftly swooping upon that tree frequented by thousands of birds, the best of birds — his body like a mountain — shook it with great speed and broke that branch, thickly covered with dense leaves.

sanskrit: sūta uvāca spṛṣṭamātrā tu padbhyāṃ sā garuḍena balīyasā abhajyata taroḥ śākhā bhagnāṃ cainām adhārayat
english: Sūta said: The moment Garuḍa, so mighty, touched it with his feet, that branch of the tree snapped — and he caught hold of it as it broke.

sanskrit: tāṃ bhagnāṃ sa mahāśākhāṃ smayan samavalokayan athātra lambato 'paśyad vālakhilyān adhomukhān
english: Gazing and smiling at that broken great branch, he then saw the Vālakhilya sages hanging from it, head downward.

sanskrit: sa tadvināśasaṃtrāsād anupatya khagādhipaḥ śākhām āsyena jagrāha teṣām evānvavekṣayā śanaiḥ paryapatat pakṣī parvatān praviśātayan
english: Out of fear of causing their destruction, the lord of birds swooped down, seized the branch in his beak out of concern for them, and flew gently, threading his way through the mountains.

sanskrit: evaṃ so 'bhyapatad deśān bahūn sagajakacchapaḥ dayārthaṃ vālakhilyānāṃ na ca sthānam avindata
english: Thus he flew over many regions, carrying the elephant and tortoise, out of compassion for the Vālakhilyas, yet found no place to set down.

sanskrit: sa gatvā parvataśreṣṭhaṃ gandhamādanam avyayam dadarśa kaśyapaṃ tatra pitaraṃ tapasi sthitam
english: Going to Gandhamādana, the foremost and imperishable of mountains, he there saw Kaśyapa, his father, standing in austerity.

sanskrit: dadarśa taṃ pitā cāpi divyarūpaṃ vihaṃgamam tejovīryabalopetaṃ manomārutaraṃhasam
english: His father too beheld that bird of divine form, endowed with splendour, heroism, and strength, swift as the mind and the wind.

sanskrit: śailaśṛṅgapratīkāśaṃ brahmadaṇḍam ivodyatam acintyam anabhijñeyaṃ sarvabhūtabhayaṃkaram
english: He resembled a mountain peak, like Brahmā's staff raised on high — inconceivable, unrecognisable in form, terrifying to all beings.

sanskrit: māyāvīryadharaṃ sākṣād agnim iddham ivodyatam apradhṛṣyam ajeyaṃ ca devadānavarākṣasaiḥ
english: He bore within him a valour like magic, like a blazing fire raised aloft — not to be assailed, not to be conquered by gods, dānavas, or rākṣasas.

sanskrit: bhettāraṃ giriśṛṅgāṇāṃ nadījalaviśoṣaṇam lokasaṃloḍanaṃ ghoraṃ kṛtāntasamadarśanam
english: He was a cleaver of mountain peaks, a drainer of river waters, a terrible churner of the worlds, dreadful to behold as Death itself.

sanskrit: tam āgatam abhiprekṣya bhagavān kaśyapas tadā viditvā cāsya saṃkalpam idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Seeing him arrive and knowing his intention, the blessed Kaśyapa then spoke these words:

sanskrit: putra mā sāhasaṃ kārṣīr mā sadyo lapsyase vyathām mā tvā daheyuḥ saṃkruddhā vālakhilyā marīcipāḥ
english: "Son, do not act rashly; do not bring sudden pain upon yourself. May the Vālakhilyas who feed on rays of light and who are fiercely wrathful not burn you."

sanskrit: prasādayām āsa sa tān kaśyapaḥ putrakāraṇāt vālakhilyāṃs tapaḥsiddhān idam uddiśya kāraṇam
english: Then Kaśyapa, for the sake of his son, appeased those Vālakhilyas who had perfected their austerities, pointing to this reason:

sanskrit: prajāhitārtham ārambho garuḍasya tapodhanāḥ cikīrṣati mahat karma tad anujñātum arhatha
english: "O wealth-of-austerity sages, Garuḍa's undertaking is for the benefit of all living beings. He desires to accomplish a great deed — you should grant him your permission."

sanskrit: evam uktā bhagavatā munayas te samabhyayuḥ muktvā śākhāṃ giriṃ puṇyaṃ himavantaṃ taporthinaḥ
english: Thus addressed by the blessed one, those sages agreed. Releasing the branch, those ascetics then made for the sacred Himavat mountain.

sanskrit: tatas teṣv apayāteṣu pitaraṃ vinatātmajaḥ śākhāvyākṣiptavadanaḥ paryapṛcchata kaśyapam
english: Then, when they had departed, the son of Vinatā — his face still occupied by the branch held in his beak — questioned his father Kaśyapa.

sanskrit: bhagavan kva vimuñcāmi taruśākhām imām aham varjitaṃ brāhmaṇair deśam ākhyātu bhagavān mama
english: "O blessed one, where shall I release this tree branch? Let the blessed one tell me of a region free from brahmins."

sanskrit: tato niṣpuruṣaṃ śailaṃ himasaṃruddhakandaram agamyaṃ manasāpy anyais tasyācakhyau sa kaśyapaḥ
english: Then Kaśyapa pointed out to him a mountain devoid of people, its ravines sealed by snow, inaccessible even to the mind of others.

sanskrit: taṃ parvatamahākukṣim āviśya manasā khagaḥ javenābhyapatat tārkṣyaḥ saśākhāgajakacchapaḥ
english: Entering the vast hollow of that mountain with the speed of thought, Tārkṣya flew swiftly, bearing the branch along with the elephant and tortoise.

sanskrit: na tāṃ vadhraḥ pariṇahec chatacarmā mahān aṇuḥ śākhino mahatīṃ śākhāṃ yāṃ pragṛhya yayau khagaḥ
english: Not even a hundred large or small leather thongs could encircle that great branch of the tree which the bird had seized and carried away.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa śatasāhasraṃ yojanāntaram āgataḥ kālena nātimahatā garuḍaḥ patatāṃ varaḥ
english: Then Garuḍa, best among fliers, covered a distance of one hundred thousand yojanas in no very great time.

sanskrit: sa taṃ gatvā kṣaṇenaiva parvataṃ vacanāt pituḥ amuñcan mahatīṃ śākhāṃ sasvanāṃ tatra khecaraḥ
english: Reaching that mountain in a mere moment, following his father's words, the sky-ranger released that great branch there with a resounding crash.

sanskrit: pakṣānilahataś cāsya prākampata sa śailarāṭ mumoca puṣpavarṣaṃ ca samāgalitapādapaḥ
english: Struck by the wind of his wings, the king of mountains trembled; the trees, shaken all together, showered down a rain of flowers.

sanskrit: śṛṅgāṇi ca vyaśīryanta gires tasya samantataḥ maṇikāñcanacitrāṇi śobhayanti mahāgirim
english: And the peaks of that mountain shattered on all sides — those peaks of jewels and gold, which adorned the great mountain.

sanskrit: śākhino bahavaś cāpi śākhayābhihatās tayā kāñcanaiḥ kusumair bhānti vidyutvanta ivāmbudāḥ
english: Many of the trees, struck by that branch, shone with their golden blossoms like clouds lit by lightning.

sanskrit: te hemavikacā bhūyo yuktāḥ parvatadhātubhiḥ vyarājañ śākhinas tatra sūryāṃśupratirañjitāḥ
english: Those trees, blazing with golden blossoms and mingled with the minerals of the mountain, shone there, reflecting the rays of the sun.

sanskrit: tatas tasya gireḥ śṛṅgam āsthāya sa khagottamaḥ bhakṣayām āsa garuḍas tāv ubhau gajakacchapau
english: Then, alighting on the peak of that mountain, Garuḍa — best of birds — devoured both the elephant and the tortoise.

sanskrit: tataḥ parvatakūṭāgrād utpapāta manojavaḥ prāvartantātha devānām utpātā bhayavedinaḥ
english: Then he launched himself from the summit of the mountain peak with the speed of thought. Thereupon ill omens arose among the gods, portending fear.

sanskrit: indrasya vajraṃ dayitaṃ prajajvāla vyathānvitam sadhūmā cāpatat sārcir divolkā nabhasaś cyutā
english: Indra's beloved thunderbolt blazed with anguish, and a heavenly meteor with smoke and flame fell from the sky.

sanskrit: tathā vasūnāṃ rudrāṇām ādityānāṃ ca sarvaśaḥ sādhyānāṃ marutāṃ caiva ye cānye devatāgaṇāḥ svaṃ svaṃ praharaṇaṃ teṣāṃ parasparam upādravat
english: And so too the weapons of the Vasus, Rudras, Ādityas in their entirety, the Sādhyas, the Maruts, and whatever other hosts of gods — each one's weapon turned against the others.

sanskrit: abhūtapūrvaṃ saṃgrāme tadā devāsure 'pi ca vavur vātāḥ sanirghātāḥ petur ulkāḥ samantataḥ
english: Something unprecedented even in the war of gods and asuras then occurred: violent thundering winds blew, and meteors fell on every side.

sanskrit: nirabhram api cākāśaṃ prajagarja mahāsvanam devānām api yo devaḥ so 'py avarṣad asṛk tadā
english: Even the cloudless sky roared with tremendous sound, and the god who is the divine dispenser of rain rained down blood.

sanskrit: mamlur mālyāni devānāṃ śemus tejāṃsi caiva hi utpātameghā raudrāś ca vavarṣuḥ śoṇitaṃ bahu rajāṃsi mukuṭāny eṣām utthitāni vyadharṣayan
english: The garlands of the gods withered, their splendours grew dim; dreadful portent-clouds rained down much blood, and dust rose up to assail their crowns.

sanskrit: tatas trāsasamudvignaḥ saha devaiḥ śatakratuḥ utpātān dāruṇān paśyann ity uvāca bṛhaspatim
english: Then Śatakratu, greatly agitated with fear, seeing these dreadful omens together with the gods, spoke thus to Bṛhaspati:

sanskrit: kimarthaṃ bhagavan ghorā mahotpātāḥ samutthitāḥ na ca śatruṃ prapaśyāmi yudhi yo naḥ pradharṣayet
english: "Why, O blessed one, have these terrible great omens arisen? And I see no enemy in battle who could challenge us."

sanskrit: bṛhaspatir uvāca tavāparādhād devendra pramādāc ca śatakrato tapasā vālakhilyānāṃ bhūtam utpannam adbhutam
english: Bṛhaspati said: "Through your transgression, O Devendra, and through your carelessness, O Śatakratu, a wondrous being has arisen through the austerities of the Vālakhilyas."

sanskrit: kaśyapasya muneḥ putro vinatāyāś ca khecaraḥ hartuṃ somam anuprāpto balavān kāmarūpavān
english: "The son of the sage Kaśyapa and of Vinatā, a flyer, powerful and capable of assuming any form, has arrived with intent to steal the soma."

sanskrit: samartho balināṃ śreṣṭho hartuṃ somaṃ vihaṃgamaḥ sarvaṃ saṃbhāvayāmy asminn asādhyam api sādhayet
english: "This bird, the foremost of the mighty, is capable of stealing the soma. I consider him capable of everything — he could even accomplish what is thought impossible."

sanskrit: sūta uvāca śrutvaitad vacanaṃ śakraḥ provācāmṛtarakṣiṇaḥ mahāvīryabalaḥ pakṣī hartuṃ somam ihodyataḥ
english: Sūta said: Having heard these words, Śakra addressed the guardians of the amṛta: "A bird of great heroism and strength is here set on stealing the soma."

sanskrit: yuṣmān saṃbodhayāmy eṣa yathā sa na hared balāt atulaṃ hi balaṃ tasya bṛhaspatir uvāca me
english: "I am alerting you so that he may not carry it off by force. Bṛhaspati has told me that his strength is matchless."

sanskrit: tac chrutvā vibudhā vākyaṃ vismitā yatnam āsthitāḥ parivāryāmṛtaṃ tasthur vajrī cendraḥ śatakratuḥ
english: Hearing these words, the gods were astonished and took up their effort; they stood surrounding the amṛta, and Indra the thunderbolt-wielder, Śatakratu, stood among them.

sanskrit: dhārayanto mahārhāṇi kavacāni manasvinaḥ kāñcanāni vicitrāṇi vaiḍūryavikṛtāni ca
english: Those high-minded ones wore their most precious armour — golden and variegated, set with vaiḍūrya gems —

sanskrit: vividhāni ca śastrāṇi ghorarūpāṇy anekaśaḥ śitatīkṣṇāgradhārāṇi samudyamya sahasraśaḥ
english: — and they raised up manifold weapons of terrible appearance, innumerable, sharp and keen of point and edge, by the thousands.

sanskrit: savisphuliṅgajvālāni sadhūmāni ca sarvaśaḥ cakrāṇi parighāṃś caiva triśūlāni paraśvadhān
english: Everywhere blazing with sparks and flames, emitting smoke — discs, iron clubs, tridents, and battle-axes —

sanskrit: śaktīś ca vividhās tīkṣṇāḥ karavālāṃś ca nirmalān svadeharūpāṇy ādāya gadāś cograpradarśanāḥ
english: — and various sharp spears, and bright swords, in forms that matched their own bodies, and maces fierce to behold —

sanskrit: taiḥ śastrair bhānumadbhis te divyābharaṇabhūṣitāḥ bhānumantaḥ suragaṇās tasthur vigatakalmaṣāḥ
english: — armed with those radiant weapons, adorned with divine ornaments, those shining hosts of gods stood free from all impurity.

sanskrit: anupamabalavīryatejaso; dhṛtamanasaḥ parirakṣaṇe 'mṛtasya asurapuravidāraṇāḥ surā; jvalanasamiddhavapuḥprakāśinaḥ
english: Those gods — of incomparable strength, heroism, and splendour — their minds set on guarding the amṛta, destroyers of the cities of the asuras, shone with bodies blazing like kindled fire.

sanskrit: iti samaravaraṃ surāsthitaṃ; parighasahasraśataiḥ samākulam vigalitam iva cāmbarāntare; tapanamarīcivibhāsitaṃ babhau
english: Thus that excellent battle-array of the gods — crowded with hundreds of thousands of iron clubs, shining within the expanse of the sky as if it were the sun's own radiance — blazed forth in glory.
